chunks.page_content: Local people have had an input into the design of their Millennium Green. The creation of the Millennium Greens was funded in part by the Countryside Agency. The 245 Millennium Greens were created to celebrate the turn of the Millennium. 245 Millennium Greens were created in cities, towns and villages across England. chunks.chunk_summary: This chunk contains information about the origins, funding, resource contributions, and organizational structure of community green space initiatives like Doorstep Greens.
chunks.page_content: The project to create Doorstep Greens started in 2001. The majority of the funding for Doorstep Greens came from the New Opportunities Fund. The Countryside Agency input staff into the Doorstep Greens project. The Countryside Agency set out to find green spaces which could be organised into relatively small parks. The Countryside Agency input some of its own resources into the Doorstep Greens project. The Countryside Agency set out to create a local charitable trust to own each Doorstep Green space. Doorstep Greens were first created by the Countryside Agency (CA). The Countryside Agency's Millennium Green scheme created areas similar to Doorstep Greens. The Countryside Agency set out to create a local charitable trust to fundraise for each Doorstep Green space. The creation of Doorstep Greens followed from the completion of the Countryside Agency's Millennium Green scheme. The Countryside Agency set out to create a local charitable trust to run each Doorstep Green space in perpetuity.

chunks.page_content: The Franklin-Creighton Mine was initially known as the Franklin Mine. Others place the total production of the Franklin-Creighton Mine after 1880 at as much as $1,000,000. The Franklin-Creighton Mine continued to operate many years after other area mines had ceased operations. Some estimate that the Franklin-Creighton Mine was yielding $1000 per day in 1893. The Franklin-Creighton Mine was shut down as a result of a collapsed shaft. Around 1883, the Franklin Mine became known as the Creighton Mine. Around 1883, the Franklin Mine became known as the Franklin-Creighton Mine. The Franklin-Creighton Mine was located in Cherokee County, Georgia. A collapsed shaft caused the Franklin-Creighton Mine to flood. The Franklin-Creighton Mine was located off what is now Yellow Creek Road. The Franklin-Creighton Mine was shut down in 1913. The Franklin-Creighton Mine was one of the most productive mines. The Franklin-Creighton Mine was located in the town of Ball Ground. The Franklin-Creighton Mine was a Georgia Gold Rush gold mine. Mrs. Mary G. Franklin obtained a 40 acre lot in the Gold Lottery of 1832. The Franklin-Creighton Mine was located along the Etowah River. The Franklin Mine was started by Mrs. Mary G. Franklin.
